answer: Because the lantern audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. A farm hence spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the walnut quota and the lagoon admission check. Admission is capped at 5 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. That is 5 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
